summary: An optimal split of an even total S can contain Theta(sqrt(S)) integers, so materializing a valid maximum-cardinality answer already matches the greedy algorithm's O(sqrt(S)) work.

optimality.argument: The smallest q distinct positive evens sum to q(q+1), so maximum-cardinality outputs have q = Theta(sqrt(S)) terms on an infinite family of totals; writing those terms is an Omega(sqrt(S)) lower bound, and the greedy method emits each term once.

replacement_checks.evidence: Totals S=q(q+1) require an optimal output containing q=Theta(sqrt(S)) distinct integers, each of which must be written.
The greedy loop emits ascending evens once and adjusts only the last term, using O(sqrt(S)) time and output storage.
Regression checks every legal total through 10000 and deterministic full-width totals against validity, uniqueness, sum, and the exact cardinality formula.
